Do not return hashes; the host binds immutable hashes.", "context": {"title": "David Copperfield", "unit": 44, "heading": "CHAPTER 42. MISCHIEF", "previous_rows": [{"source_id": "en85-u044-b0158", "target": "Он с гордостью возобновил своё право в часы досуга прогуливаться по саду взад и вперёд вместе с доктором, как привык ходить по Докторской дорожке в Кентербери. Но едва дела приняли такой оборот, как он посвятил этим прогулкам всё своё свободное время (и вставал пораньше, чтобы его стало больше). Если прежде он никогда не бывал так счастлив, как когда доктор читал ему это удивительное творение — Словарь, то теперь он был совершенно несчастен, если доктор не вытаскивал его из кармана и не начинал. Когда мы с доктором занимались, он теперь взял обыкновение ходить взад и вперёд с миссис Стронг и помогать ей подрезать любимые цветы или полоть грядки. Смею сказать, он редко произносил и дюжину слов в час; но его тихая участливость и задумчивое лицо находили немедленный отклик в сердцах обоих; каждый знал, что другой его любит, и что он любит обоих; и он стал тем, чем не мог быть никто другой, — связующим звеном между ними.", "source_sha256": "9145d27fdd8b52f8681c4bc451df9c15b18e6f9d3a5ce4df7b0e5ba619978e2e", "target_id": "ru-en85-u044-b0158", "tag": "p", "target_sha256": "b18efda532e376c0187193e49ad919468f2303054894d69df58c5576a21625a4"}, {"source_id": "en85-u044-b0159", "target": "Когда я думаю о нём, с его непроницаемо мудрым лицом, шагающем взад и вперёд с доктором, довольном тем, что трудные слова Словаря молотят его, как цепы; когда я думаю о нём, несущем огромные лейки вслед за Энни; стоящем на коленях, в перчатках, похожих на лапы, за терпеливой, почти микроскопической работой среди маленьких листочков; выражающем, как не мог бы выразить ни один философ, во всём, что он делал, деликатное желание быть её другом; изливающем сочувствие, доверие и привязанность из каждой дырочки лейки; когда я думаю о нём, никогда не блуждающем в том лучшем уме, к которому обращалось несчастье, никогда не приводящем в сад злополучного короля Карла, никогда не колеблющемся в своей благодарной службе, никогда не отвлекающемся от знания, что что-то неладно, и от желания всё исправить, — мне, право, почти стыдно, что я знал, будто он не совсем в здравом уме, если принять в расчёт всё, что я сделал своим собственным.", "source_sha256": "63a3cc9d8db4a0fe88f28a5ce6b1362da140d91b5fa9005a73c645fa6a77437b", "target_id": "ru-en85-u044-b0159", "tag": "p", "target_sha256": "712efc236dc4c1c25de089312b3605bb60524b375d8757710491bc10f8ad195f"}], "source_language": "English", "part": null, "book": null, "chapter": 42, "role": "chapter"}, "source_rows": [{"id": "en85-u044-b0160", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Nobody but myself, Trot, knows what that man is!’ my aunt would proudly remark, when we conversed about it. ‘Dick will distinguish himself yet!’", "sha256": "54573a49be86e99861c505bb25c04975f0d06d90aa072bb210e39724440ee366", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[49]/p[160]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u044-b0161", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "I must refer to one other topic before I close this chapter. While the visit at the Doctor’s was still in progress, I observed that the postman brought two or three letters every morning for Uriah Heep, who remained at Highgate until the rest went back, it being a leisure time; and that these were always directed in a business-like manner by Mr. Micawber, who now assumed a round legal hand. I was glad to infer, from these slight premises, that Mr. Micawber was doing well; and consequently was much surprised to receive, about this time, the following letter from his amiable wife.", "sha256": "5abf84fcceace208eabd052dce09bbb8ce6748b5089186e2eb9c737d5d807cbe", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[49]/p[161]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u044-b0162", "tag": "p", "role": "dateline_or_signature", "text": "‘CANTERBURY, Monday Evening.", "sha256": "6892df3d7ab4e5ca310af176c4480c966556918285c70226b36eb0bee765f81c", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[49]/p[162]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": "right"}, {"id": "en85-u044-b0163", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘You will doubtless be surprised, my dear Mr. Copperfield, to receive this communication. Still more so, by its contents. Still more so, by the stipulation of implicit confidence which I beg to impose. But my feelings as a wife and mother require relief; and as I do not wish to consult my family (already obnoxious to the feelings of Mr. Micawber), I know no one of whom I can better ask advice than my friend and former lodger.", "sha256": "1ad1f5a552242b11ebf50929201a87674352a55fe261cf7196c11728a2a42127", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[49]/p[163]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u044-b0164", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘You may be aware, my dear Mr. Copperfield, that between myself and Mr. Micawber (whom I will never desert), there has always been preserved a spirit of mutual confidence. Mr. Micawber may have occasionally given a bill without consulting me, or he may have misled me as to the period when that obligation would become due. This has actually happened. But, in general, Mr. Micawber has had no secrets from the bosom of affection—I allude to his wife—and has invariably, on our retirement to rest, recalled the events of the day.", "sha256": "27df1e978c01ebe3b1abe18e79893426a8ede29003f020334136e78ee5886ccb", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[49]/p[164]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u044-b0165", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘You will picture to yourself, my dear Mr. Copperfield, what the poignancy of my feelings must be, when I inform you that Mr. Micawber is entirely changed. He is reserved. He is secret. His life is a mystery to the partner of his joys and sorrows—I again allude to his wife—and if I should assure you that beyond knowing that it is passed from morning to night at the office, I now know less of it than I do of the man in the south, connected with whose mouth the thoughtless children repeat an idle tale respecting cold plum porridge, I should adopt a popular fallacy to express an actual fact.", "sha256": "775b7930b4ccf047dd674b54b421af2cdb17c473955ee544ec9bbf326273df12", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[49]/p[165]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u044-b0166", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘But this is not all. Mr. Micawber is morose. He is severe. He is estranged from our eldest son and daughter, he has no pride in his twins, he looks with an eye of coldness even on the unoffending stranger who last became a member of our circle. The pecuniary means of meeting our expenses, kept down to the utmost farthing, are obtained from him with great difficulty, and even under fearful threats that he will Settle himself (the exact expression); and he inexorably refuses to give any explanation whatever of this distracting policy.", "sha256": "5c848b31f433f05169838309b2562ce50eb2b7caa719c016fcd169fd386ef9ba", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[49]/p[166]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u044-b0167", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘This is hard to bear. This is heart-breaking. If you will advise me, knowing my feeble powers such as they are, how you think it will be best to exert them in a dilemma so unwonted, you will add another friendly obligation to the many you have already rendered me. With loves from the children, and a smile from the happily-unconscious stranger, I remain, dear Mr. Copperfield,", "sha256": "f75556ac1fa56115491ac569c7ba9401daa146aa98cd6aa95482246be1894997", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[49]/p[167]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u044-b0168", "tag": "p", "role": "dateline_or_signature", "text": "‘Your afflicted,\n‘EMMA MICAWBER.’", "sha256": "b02957df5c6ebaff0a57162e060c4270783318e93df4b224e696e1d3e8498c1a", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[49]/p[168]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_lines": ["‘Your afflicted,", "‘EMMA MICAWBER.’"], "source_class": "right"}, {"id": "en85-u044-b0169", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "I did not feel justified in giving a wife of Mrs. Micawber’s experience any other recommendation, than that she should try to reclaim Mr. Micawber by patience and kindness (as I knew she would in any case); but the letter set me thinking about him very much.", "sha256": "1be29dd6cc2236c35ea1716ac20fdd5591384ed7fa824e6e1f469bf59bfb0cc4", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[49]/p[169]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}]}
